solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Broadcast Ella Fitzgerald? (7)

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to fling it widely
Ella Fitzgerald sang scat, so she is one who scats

annotation.surface: A radio programme playing Ella Fitzgerald records.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense is a coinage: SCAT-TER, one who sings scat, read as a new word. The question mark flags that invention.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for sending seed or news far and wide; the second sense is a coinage for a scat singer.

entries.clue: Elite soldiers start to show impertinence to Green Beret (4)

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the Special Air Service, Britain's elite regiment
surface padding: a Green Beret is a US special forces soldier

annotation.surface: British special forces cheeking an American Green Beret.
annotation.walkthrough: The SAS is the British Army's special forces regiment. 'To Green Beret' only completes the picture of rival elite soldiers; the wordplay stops at 'show'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mostly American: backchat or cheek.

entries.clue: A paper handkerchief is being discussed (2,5)

blocks.note: a paper hanky, a word beginning with T

annotation.surface: Someone talking about a paper hanky.
annotation.walkthrough: The split is the whole trick: A TISSUE, respaced, becomes AT ISSUE.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the point at issue is the one currently under debate.

entries.clue: Reportedly that place is belonging to that person (5)

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, not seen

blocks.note: that place is there; spoken, it matches the possessive

annotation.surface: Someone told that a place belongs to a certain person.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition uses singular they: the possessive can mean belonging to one person of unstated sex.
annotation.definitionFit: The singular-they possessive, standing for his or her.

entries.clue: Heavy defeat initially exposed United’s direct style of football (5,3)

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word it follows

annotation.surface: A football report: United were thrashed, their long-ball game laid bare.
annotation.walkthrough: 'United' reads as a club like Manchester United but gives ONE.
annotation.definitionFit: British football slang for the long ball hoofed straight upfield, bypassing midfield.

entries.clue: Why pull a face on the radio? Spectacular fail! (7)

indicators.note: radio is heard, so the words are taken by sound

blocks.note: why + pout (pull a face) said together

annotation.surface: A radio listener asks why a presenter bothers grimacing when nobody can see.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface joke is real: a pulled face is wasted on radio listeners, which is exactly why the sound is all that counts here.
annotation.definitionFit: Surfing slang for a heavy fall, extended to any spectacular failure.

entries.clue: Anger about second letter from Merrick Garland (6)

indicators.note: wrath goes about, around, the extra letter
says which letter of Merrick to take

annotation.surface: Someone angry about a letter from Merrick Garland, the US Attorney General.
annotation.walkthrough: Merrick Garland reads as one name, a US Attorney General; split it and Garland is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a ring of flowers or leaves, as hung on a door or laid at a memorial.

entries.clue: Stick with lap dancing before gaining work experience from this (9)

indicators.note: letters that dance move about
puts the anagram ahead of cement

annotation.surface: A lurid tale of lap dancing leading on to someone's work experience.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the whole phrase names the job a student takes to learn the ropes.
annotation.definitionFit: A description of the thing: the temporary job where a student gets work experience.

entries.clue: Examination about small section in ring road (7)

indicators.note: oral goes about, around, bit

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken exam
a bit is a small piece

annotation.surface: An exam question about one short stretch of a ring road.
annotation.walkthrough: Examination is a noun here, a spoken test, not the act of looking.
annotation.definitionFit: A British term for a motorway circling a city, as the M25 does London.

entries.clue: Perhaps Thomas Brown unusually keen to drink alcohol (4,6)

indicators.note: the letters of keen come out in an unusual order
the anagram swallows the alcohol

annotation.surface: A man called Thomas Brown, oddly eager to have a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thomas Brown' reads as one person; Thomas is the definition, Brown gives TAN. Thomas the Tank Engine is the children's-book locomotive.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Thomas in the children's books is a locomotive carrying its water in side tanks.

entries.clue: Calculator’s standard on decline (5,4)

indicators.note: rule sits on, after, slide

annotation.surface: Someone saying the calculator's standards are slipping.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the pre-electronic calculating device of engineers.

entries.clue: The first British martyr from Scotland originally? (5)

blocks.note: the saint of Verulamium, the Roman town now named after him
Alba is the old Gaelic name for Scotland; add N for 'of Alba'

annotation.surface: A question whether Britain's first martyr was originally a Scot.
annotation.walkthrough: The saint was a Roman-era Briton, not a Scot; the question mark flags the playful second sense built on Alba, Scotland.
annotation.definitionFit: A saint's name: the Roman-era Christian of Verulamium, traditionally Britain's first martyr; the second sense is 'of Alba'.

entries.clue: Plays outside in small box, perhaps; pressure on to keep dry (6,7)

indicators.note: tree follows small, as a thing in a place
dry comes before the pressure it keeps back

blocks.note: box is a kind of evergreen shrub
putting the heat on is applying pressure

annotation.surface: Children playing out in a small box, told to keep under cover.
annotation.walkthrough: Box here is the hedging shrub, not a container. TT (teetotal) is the standard crossword 'dry'.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: drama performed in public spaces rather than in a building.

entries.clue: Rank those people on boat, which is wrong (3,3,4)

indicators.note: those people and boat follow rank

annotation.surface: Grading passengers aboard a boat is deemed unfair.
annotation.walkthrough: Rank looks like a verb or a position; here it is the adjective meaning foul-smelling.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from shooting or racing: wide of the target, so wrong.

entries.clue: Patronise monarch heartlessly, overwhelmed by worry (8)

indicators.note: removes the middle letter
the monarch is buried inside the worry

blocks.note: fret = worry; it wraps round: FRE(...)T

annotation.surface: Someone talking down to a monarch while anxiety gets the better of them.
annotation.walkthrough: Patronise here means be a patron of, a regular customer, not talk down to.
annotation.definitionFit: Patronise in its shop sense, to be a regular customer of.

entries.clue: Harry found her appalling at first — that’s without precedent (7-2)

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so the letters are knocked about
takes the first letter of appalling

annotation.surface: Prince Harry found some woman appalling, which is unprecedented.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Harry' reads as the prince, so the anagram indicator hides as a name at the start.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: so unusual nobody has known it happen before.

entries.clue: Penny says to collect large walking aid (3,3)

indicators.note: the two says gather up the L between them

blocks.note: say = e.g., so two of them

annotation.surface: A woman called Penny tells someone to pick up a large walking stick.
annotation.walkthrough: Penny reads as a name and 'says' as speech; 'says' is the plural of say, e.g., hence two EGs.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a wooden leg, the pirate's classic walking aid.

entries.clue: Chief in California turned up on a list (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up turns the letters backwards

blocks.note: list = tip, lean over, as a ship lists

annotation.surface: A chief in California showed up on some list.
annotation.walkthrough: List is the nautical lean, a tip, not a register.
annotation.definitionFit: The Italian word for captain, used in English for a chief or head man.

entries.clue: Decline to get rid of American memorial (6)

indicators.note: the wasting word disposes of the A

annotation.surface: Someone refusing to scrap an American memorial.
annotation.walkthrough: Decline reads as refuse; it is the noun or verb for wasting away.
annotation.definitionFit: An old sense: a monument or spoils kept in memory of a victory.

entries.clue: Abandoned cat in tree beginning to eat biscuit (7)

indicators.note: letters let loose get rearranged
the anagram goes inside the tree
takes the first letter of eat

blocks.note: oak tree; it wraps round: O(...)AK

annotation.surface: A stray cat up a tree starts nibbling a biscuit.
annotation.walkthrough: Abandoned looks like 'deserted' describing the cat; it is the anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a flat Scottish oat biscuit.

entries.clue: Intended leaving European country, frankly (3,2,3)

indicators.note: something leaving a place is no longer in it, so the E departs from the word for intended

annotation.surface: Someone frankly admitting they meant to leave a European country.
annotation.walkthrough: Leaving looks like departing a country; it only takes E out of meant.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: speaking openly and honestly, as between equals.

entries.clue: Mother, charming individual, cycling in expensive area of London (7)

indicators.note: the last letter cycles round to the front

blocks.note: a fairy casts charms; cycled: Y moves to the front

annotation.surface: A mother and a charming person cycling round posh London.
annotation.walkthrough: Cycling reads as riding a bike through the streets; it moves the last letter to the front.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a wealthy district of central London, the dearest square on the British Monopoly board.

entries.clue: Smart bishop not mistaken (6)

annotation.surface: A clever bishop who is never wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: Bishop looks like a churchman; here it is just the chess abbreviation B.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for clever, quick-witted.

entries.clue: Remarkable X-ray editor ran is fake (13)

indicators.note: a fake version of the letters is a false arrangement

annotation.surface: A newspaper story: a remarkable X-ray the editor printed was a fake.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's odd grammar is the clue: 'ran is fake' only makes sense once you see the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: beyond the ordinary, worthy of remark.

entries.clue: Woman possibly read ultimatum, but not from start to finish (5)

indicators.text: but not from start to finish
indicators.note: take letters from the phrase but not the whole of it, first to last

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of read into the start of ultimatum

annotation.surface: A woman reading an ultimatum, but only part of it.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'possibly' is needed: a woman is only one kind of grown-up.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a woman is one kind of grown-up, hence possibly.

entries.clue: Glorify going topless? Not so much (4)

indicators.note: the top letter, in a down clue, goes

blocks.note: to bless God is to glorify him; then lose B

annotation.surface: A sniffy verdict on going topless: glorify it less, please.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Topless' is a cheeky surface; in a down clue it means lose the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: The comparative of little: a smaller amount, not so much.

entries.clue: 17? A child (5)

blocks.note: a child under a guardian's care

annotation.walkthrough: 17 refers to the answer at 17 across, TROPHY; a trophy is one kind of prize, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example via cross-reference: 17 across is a trophy, which is one kind of prize.

entries.clue: Make rough old woman wail when leading couple ejected (9)

indicators.note: the first two letters are thrown out

annotation.surface: A grandmother howling as the dancing couple in front are thrown out.
annotation.walkthrough: Make rough looks like roughing someone up; it is the technical sense of giving a grainy surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical sense: to give a surface a grainy, roughened texture.

entries.clue: Secretly look around motor racing track’s entrance for health programme (4,3)

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the other way, so the look is read backwards
the entrance of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: F1, Formula One, with the 1 read as I

annotation.surface: A spy sneaking round a motor-racing circuit's gate, supposedly for their health.
annotation.walkthrough: F1 becomes FI: the numeral 1 is used as the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: A set name: British exercise classes aimed at staying healthy.

entries.clue: Equal working conditions (2,5)

blocks.note: a machine that's on is working

annotation.surface: A demand for equal working conditions.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about fair pay; split, each word does its own job.
annotation.definitionFit: A sporting idiom: a side that has pulled back to level pegging is equal again.
